thread:
alex: Heads-up 1 Is anyone opposed to exposing a small Cursor object in the SDKs instead of only a raw resume token string? Rationale: Cursor can hold helper methods (next_page(), to_token()) and implement language iterator patterns. We still keep the token opaque under the hood. Thoughts?

noor: I like Cursor as a first-class primitive. It makes prefetching and cancellation ergonomic. But we must be strict about the token being opaque bytestring so server can change encoding. Cursor.to_token() -> string for passing around.

rachel: +1. A Cursor lets us add helpers like cursor.prefetch(n) or cursor.peek() without changing server contract. Concern: how do we handle retries if a page has side effects? We can't naively retry entire call ranges.

kevin: For side-effecting endpoints we need an explicit idempotency strategy. Options: 1) require an Idempotency-Key header for mutating paged ops, 2) require server to mark pages as "commit points" and only replay to last commit point. I prefer (2) because it keeps client simpler.

alex: I want to avoid forcing callers to manage headers. If server emits commit markers in responses (last_committed_token) clients can safely resume to that point. Cursor abstraction can expose commit_token() separately from transient continuation_token().

noor: Implementation-wise: Cursor is just a tiny wrapper around token + metadata. Py/TS can implement Cursor as an async iterable; Go will expose a struct with Next(ctx) (returns items, token, err) and a Channel() helper for idiomatic usage.

kevin: Example Go shape I sketched:
```go
type Cursor struct { token string }
func (c *Cursor) Next(ctx context.Context) ([]Item, string, error) { /* unary fetch */ }
func (c *Cursor) Stream(ctx context.Context) (<-chan Item, <-chan error) { /* optional helper that spins a goroutine */ }
```
We should document that Stream() is a convenience and backpressure is the caller's responsibility.

rachel: For Python: Cursor as AsyncIterator + sync wrapper seems good. Also expose cursor.commit_token and cursor.to_token.

alex: Another dimension: prefetch window. We could default to lazy (no prefetch) but give cursor.prefetch(n) to fetch next n pages opportunistically. This helps small page latency without surprising memory usage. Should prefetch be opt-in?

noor: Opt-in by default. Maybe an API like cursor.with_prefetch(n, max_bytes=...). Otherwise people hit OOM in browsers.

kevin: Transport & streaming interplay: grpc-stream vs http-chunk vs websocket. For paging/unary Cursor calls http chunking or simple JSON over HTTP is fine. For live generation streaming keep a separate stream API. Don't try to multiplex both over the Cursor.

rachel: Agree separate APIs. Also cancellation semantics for streaming: we need to define whether cancelling a client stream implicitly signals server to stop generation and discard partial state. That should be a per-call flag ("cancel_and_abort"). Default should ask server to stop work.

alex: Retry semantics: let's expose a middleware-stack approach where retries are pluggable. Default retry for paging: transient network errors replay up to last committed token; server returns "unreplayable" for pages that cannot be retried. For idempotent read-only paging allow automatic replay.

noor: We should standardize error codes: PAGING_TOKEN_INVALID, PAGING_NOT_RESUMABLE, PAGING_COMMIT_REQUIRED, STREAM_CANCELLED. SDKs translate these to typed exceptions so apps can branch.

infra-bot: reminder: please add integration tests for Cursor roundtrip (to_token -> from_token) and for prefetch memory bounds. Tagging @alex @rachel.

kevin: One more: telemetry. Cursor operations should emit fine-grained metrics: pages_fetched, prefetch_pages, resume_attempts, resume_success. This helps Optimize recommendations later.

rachel: UX question: expose raw token in high-level UI? I think hide by default but provide cursor.to_token() for app-level persistence. Note: token strings must be stable across minor server restarts but may be invalidated by major model changes. Document that.

alex: Action items: noor will draft Cursor API sketches for Py/TS/Go, kevin will add error-code list and telemetry keys, rachel will write a short doc about prefetch safety and streaming cancel flags. I'll consolidate into an RFC next week. Thanks. :rocket:
